newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan likes Iraq oil price, shoots for 40,000 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Japan likes Iraq oil price, shoots for 40,000 bpd.

text.p: Japan refiners are lined up to take Iraqi crude volumes on the order of 40,000 barrels per day (bpd), Tokyo oil traders said on Wednesday, adding that buyers are largely satisfied with Iraq's latest price formula.
In a proposal submitted to the United Nations on Tuesday, Iraq's Basrah Light to Asian buyers was offered at an average of Oman/Dubai crudes minus 55 cents per barrel on a free-on-board (FOB) basis.

The crude's value is unchanged from the terms in the first 180 days of Iraqi sales -- still a relative bargain compared to its Saudi counterpart, Arabian Light, which is priced at parity with the Oman/Dubai average for August.

"This is a fair price, and it's quite likely that Mitsubishi will try to roll-over (its contract) at its previous 20,000 bpd volumes, with Idemitsu and Cosmo each taking about 10,000 bpd," said a crude trader with a Japanese refiner.
Traders said a representative from Japan's Mitsubishi Corp was now in Baghdad negotiating with Iraq's State Oil and Marketing Organisation (SOMO).
The Japanese trading giant is operating on behalf of refiners Nippon Oil, Japan Energy Corp, Kashima Oil Co and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd, they said.
Japan refiners Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd and Cosmo Oil Ltd are each looking to secure Basrah Light volumes independently.
U.N. overseers are expected to formally recommend the Iraqi price to the Security Council's sanctions committee on Iraq sometime on Wednesday morning in New York, diplomats said.
The committee then has 48 hours to raise any objections to the formula, or it automatically becomes valid.
Japan traders said their appetite for the grade was robust, and only limited by a lack of spot market availability.
"During the first 180 days of sales we took a total of 900,000 barrels from Iraq, but really we have more appetite than that," said one Japan trader.
"We would really like more spot barrels, but of course Iraq doesn't have discretion to allocate spot volumes," he said.
One proviso of the U.N. food-for-oil deal is that end-users of purchased Iraqi material be strictly specified in the original contract, making spot trade of the barrels illicit.
"Before the (Gulf War) happened, we had a term contract for Basrah -- we would like that to resume," the trader added.
Basrah Light, with an American Petroleum Institute (API) gravity of 34.4, is a light Mideast grade similar in quality to Saudi Arabian Light.
It is produced by Iraq's state-owned Southern Oil Co.
The grade loads from the Persian Gulf terminal at Mina al-Bakr, which has an estimated capacity of 300,000 to 500,000 barrel per day.

U.N. resolution 986 allows Iraq to sell $2.14 billion worth of over a 180-day period which began June 8. Of the total, $2 billion is allotted for the purchase of food and medicine for Iraqi citizens, as well as war reparations.
An additional $140 million is allowed for pipeline costs. -- Tokyo Energy Desk +813-5473-3708
